title: Errors with fingerprints: the same failure is one group, written where it is caught, under its request and job
request: Phase 1's fourth gap: every error in the record with a fingerprint (the exception's type and the top frame inside our code), the request, the job or run it belongs to; a rate-limit refusal as an event; the Sessions page and the command line grouping the last days by fingerprint; adoptable by the main product.
spec: dclab_core.errors.fingerprint and from_exception; error.raised with fingerprint, frame and status, stage.failed with fingerprint and frame (the contract at v5); written by the API's exception handler, the limit refusal, the job runner, the stage runner, the draft pipeline and the intern; finder.errors groups; GET /api/experience/errors, the CLI's errors command, an Admin table.
plan: Put the fingerprint in dclab_core: type and the innermost frame of our own code, twelve hex characters, a host adds its own package prefixes.
Add the fields to the two error kinds and move the contract to v5.
Write it where each failure is caught, under the ids already bound there (the job's visit and request through _acting).
Group in the finder; expose on the route, the CLI and the Admin page.
Test the fingerprint, the grouping, a failed stage through the runner's own branch and a failed job through the worker.

decisions.decision: The fingerprint is the exception's type and the innermost frame inside our own packages, never the message.
decisions.why: A message quotes values and paths; two projects failing the same way must be one group, and nothing of a table may enter a meta field.

decisions.decision: An error raised outside our code groups by its type alone.
decisions.why: A library's frame changes with its version; the type is what the owner can act on.

decisions.decision: The job runner writes error.raised inside _acting, before job.stopped.
decisions.why: That is where the job's visit, request and id are bound; the done-when asks for the request id beside the group.

decisions.decision: A limit refusal is an error.raised with status 429 and the limit's kind as where, written explicitly to the workspace's log.
decisions.why: It is answered before the visit is bound; the Sessions page should still show a person hitting a limit.

decisions.decision: The contract moves to v5 for two meta fields.
decisions.why: The rule from 23.2's review: a kind's fields are part of the contract's shape; older versions read as the current one.

change: dclab_core errors.py (new), experience.py (fields, v5), CHANGELOG 0.41.0, schemas; dclab_rnd agentic/server.py (500 and 429), jobs/worker.py, studio/engine.py, experience/hooks.py, draft/pipeline.py, intern/loop.py, experience/finder.py (errors), experience/__main__.py (errors), agentic/pages/sessions.py (GET /api/experience/errors), accounts/guard.py, web admin.html (the table); tests test_errors.py (new), test_experience_finder, test_lineage, test_core_experience, the wheel check; CORE_INTEGRATION.md, the plan.

findings.defect: The stage test mocked the stage runner itself and so skipped its own failure branch.
findings.scenario: No stage.failed event: the except is inside _run_stage.
findings.cause: The mock sat above the branch under test.
findings.fix: The test mocks prepare and the data step inside the runner's try.

findings.defect: The engine's public execute is behind the workflow graph: a project without a saved solution is blocked at WF-01 before any stage runs.
findings.fix: The test enters at _execute, past the gate, which is not what it measures.

findings.defect: The errors route raised NameError: the finder was imported in the module's helpers, not in register.
findings.scenario: GET /api/experience/errors answered 500 in the API contract test.
findings.cause: A local import pattern in the file.

findings.defect: The job test expected the test's own frame; the innermost frame of ours is the worker's execute.
findings.scenario: A handler outside our packages fails: the group rests on the worker's frame.

findings.defect: Only the requests-a-minute 429 of the middleware was an event; the 429s raised through services.over_limit (uploads, jobs at once, model spend) were not.
findings.scenario: A person at the daily upload allowance uploads again: 429, nothing in the record, nothing on the Errors table.
findings.cause: The event was written in one branch instead of where every limit refusal is made.
findings.fix: services.limit_hit writes it; over_limit calls it and the middleware passes the workspace's log and the person.
findings.test: test_limits test_upload_bytes (the 429 event where limit:upload_bytes, status 429)

findings.defect: A stage failing inside a job was counted twice: the engine's stage.failed and the worker's error.raised share the exception.
findings.scenario: One failed stage job shows Times 2 on the Admin page; every real count was doubled for the package's own done-when scenario.
findings.cause: The group counted events, not failures.
findings.fix: finder.errors counts one occurrence per job (or event id without a job).
findings.test: test_the_last_days_errors_group_by_fingerprint (the same failure caught twice is one count)

findings.defect: The intern's fingerprint was built from the error text and a fixed frame, so every failure of one type was one group wherever it broke, and a rule's prose became the code.
findings.scenario: A model that answered without a tool: 80 characters of a sentence hashed as the key.
findings.cause: The exception was dropped at the except and only its text kept.
findings.fix: from_exception at the except; a loop ended by a rule gets the rule's name as the code (NoToolCall).
findings.test: test_intern (unchanged behaviour) — the fingerprint's source is the exception

findings.defect: The main-product adapter emitted error.raised and stage.failed without a fingerprint, so its rows never shared the reference grouping.
findings.scenario: The finder's fallback key kept them grouped by code only.
findings.cause: The adapter was not in the change.
findings.fix: A type-only fingerprint where the main product gives a code, as the contract defines for an error outside our frames.
findings.test: test_model_invocations_decisions_and_run_boundaries (E_METRIC with a 12-character fingerprint and no frame)

findings.defect: The 500 path's new fields, the CLI's errors command and the 429 event had no assertion.
findings.scenario: A regression in any of them would pass the suite.
findings.cause: Tests written for the main path.
findings.fix: Assertions on status and fingerprint at the 500, the CLI run on a file log, the upload 429 event.

findings.defect: The gate on ac5733c failed: tests/test_experience_log.py lists every write route with what it records and did not know POST /api/experience/ui (23.2).
findings.scenario: check-commit FAILED; the log was lost to a tail and the suite was rerun with the log kept.
findings.cause: A new write route without its line in the list.
findings.fix: The route is listed with its five ui.* kinds (in this commit).

outcome: Every error in the record carries a fingerprint and sits under its request and job; the Sessions page, the route and the CLI group the last days by it; a limit hit is a group of its own. Reviewed: 5 findings fixed; every 429 is an event, one failure is one count.
lessons: Write a fingerprint where the exception is caught, never where the message is rendered: the ids are bound there and the message has not yet quoted anything.
Keep a gate's whole log in the scratchpad: a tail that loses the failing test costs a full rerun.
risks: The main product computes its fingerprints with its own package prefixes (own=); until it does, its error rows group by type alone.
The browser page's errors (ui.error_shown) carry a code, not a fingerprint: the server's error is the one grouped.
